title: Final exam
note: Approved paper, transcribed verbatim. Stems, options and keys must match the source file exactly; final-exam-content.test.ts enforces this.

sections.title: Section A — Multiple choice
sections.brief: Twenty standalone questions. Select the single best answer for each one.

sections.title: Section B — True or false
sections.brief: Five statements. Decide whether each statement is true or false.

sections.title: Section C — Shared use case
sections.brief: Read the scenario once, then answer all five questions on this page.

use_case.title: The use case
use_case.intro: An organisation has 200 policy documents. Employees use an AI assistant to ask questions about leave and travel policies.
requirements: Show the document name and page
State clearly when no approved evidence is available
Allow an employee to submit an objection
Ask for confirmation before submitting the objection
Protect documents that are private to specific departments
Continue working when many employees use it at the same time
use_case.closing: The questions begin with basic decisions and become gradually more challenging.

instructions.heading: Read this before you begin
points: This exam has 30 questions in three sections: Section A is 20 multiple-choice questions, Section B is 5 true or false statements, and Section C is 5 questions about one shared use case.
You have 50 minutes and one attempt. The clock runs on the server, so closing the page does not pause it, and the attempt cannot be reopened once submitted.
Answer every question by choosing one option. Your answers save the moment you pick them.
Use a laptop or desktop computer. The exam works on a phone but the questions are cramped and fullscreen is unavailable on iPhone.
The exam runs in fullscreen. If you leave fullscreen you have 10 seconds to return before it is recorded, so pressing Escape by accident costs you nothing.
You have 3 warnings. Leaving this page for another tab or app, staying out of fullscreen, or trying to copy or paste each record one warning.
After the 3rd warning the exam freezes and you cannot answer until an instructor unlocks it. Your clock pauses while you wait, so you lose no exam time. Raise your hand straight away.
Your score is not shown when you submit. Your instructor releases marks and explanations after the exam.

questions.stem: What does a large language model mainly do when it generates text?

options.A: Searches a trusted database for the correct sentence
options.B: Predicts the next token from the available context
options.C: Checks whether every statement is factually correct
options.D: Stores the complete conversation permanently

questions.rationale: An LLM generates text by predicting the next token from the context already available. A model does not automatically search a trusted database, the generation loop does not verify truth, and a model does not automatically store conversations permanently.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes the context window?

options.A: It is the model’s permanent memory of previous users.
options.B: It is the collection of documents used during model training.
options.C: It is the database where application records are stored.
options.D: It is the maximum text available during one model request.

questions.rationale: The context window is the maximum amount of text the model can use in one request, including instructions, history, retrieved text, the question, and the answer. Permanent memory is stored outside the model, training data is not the same as the current context, and application records belong in external storage.

questions.stem: Where should an application store an API key?

options.A: In an environment variable or secrets manager
options.B: In the system prompt sent to the model
options.C: In the application’s public user interface
options.D: In a source-code repository for easy access

questions.rationale: API keys are credentials and should be stored in environment variables or a dedicated secrets manager. The system prompt is not a secure location, a public interface would expose the key, and a key committed to a repository should be treated as compromised.

questions.stem: What does the temperature setting mainly control?

options.A: How many documents are stored in the database
options.B: How creative or predictable the model's response is
options.C: How long the API key remains active
options.D: How the application verifies user permissions

questions.rationale: Temperature controls how random or focused the model's next-token choices are: a low temperature favors the most likely, predictable tokens, and a high temperature allows more varied, creative output. It does not control document storage, key lifetime, or permission checks, which the application handles elsewhere.

questions.stem: What is the main purpose of the system message?

options.A: To store the user's permanent data
options.B: To define the model's main behavior
options.C: To execute external tools
options.D: To search the vector database

questions.rationale: The system message sets the model's role, tone, and behavior for the whole conversation. It is not where user data is stored, it does not execute tools itself, and it does not search a vector database.

questions.stem: What is the main purpose of Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG)?

options.A: To provide the model with relevant external evidence at answer time
options.B: To allow the model to execute actions in external systems
options.C: To change the model’s behavior through additional training
options.D: To store user sessions permanently inside the model

questions.rationale: RAG retrieves relevant evidence from an external knowledge source and supplies it to the model when it answers. Tools and agents support external actions, fine-tuning changes model behavior through training, and sessions are managed by the application.

questions.stem: What is an embedding?

options.A: A readable summary generated for each document
options.B: A permanent instruction stored inside the language model
options.C: A list of keywords copied from the user’s question
options.D: A numerical representation used to compare meaning

questions.rationale: An embedding is a numerical vector used to compare semantic meaning between text passages and queries. It is not a readable summary, not a model instruction, and not simply a keyword list.

questions.stem: Which search method is normally strongest for an exact reference such as HR-204?

options.A: Semantic reranking only
options.B: Random sampling from the index
options.C: Keyword search
options.D: Answer generation

questions.rationale: Keyword search is strong for exact codes, identifiers, names, and precise phrases. Reranking can improve candidate ordering but does not replace exact-term retrieval, random sampling is not a retrieval method, and generation happens after retrieval.

questions.stem: An employee searches for both an exact policy code and questions written in natural language. Which retrieval method is most appropriate?

options.A: Keyword search only
options.B: Vector search only
options.C: Hybrid search
options.D: Fine-tuning

questions.rationale: Hybrid search combines keyword matching, which is strong for exact codes and identifiers, with vector search, which is strong for natural-language meaning. Using only one method would miss the other kind of query, and fine-tuning does not address retrieval.

questions.stem: The correct passage reaches the model, but the answer adds a condition that is not present in the passage. Which area should be investigated first?

options.A: Document ingestion and file upload
options.B: Embedding dimensions and index configuration
options.C: Metadata storage and document identifiers
options.D: Generation instructions and groundedness

questions.rationale: The correct evidence was retrieved, but the model did not remain faithful to it, so this is mainly a generation or groundedness problem. The source was already ingested, the correct passage was already found, and metadata did not cause the unsupported condition.

questions.stem: An organisation approves a new policy document. What should happen before employees can retrieve it through the RAG system?

options.A: Clean, chunk, embed, and add the document to the index
options.B: Send the full document with every employee question
options.C: Ask the model to remember the document permanently
options.D: Create an objection tool for the new policy

questions.rationale: A new document must pass through the offline preparation pipeline before users can retrieve it: it is cleaned, divided into chunks, embedded, and added to the index. Sending the full document every time wastes context and cost, the model does not permanently remember documents from a request, and an objection tool is unrelated.

questions.stem: A model returns a request to call a function. Who actually executes the function?

options.A: The vector database
options.B: The system prompt
options.C: The application code
options.D: The language model itself

questions.rationale: The model returns a structured request. Application code checks it and decides whether to execute the function. A vector database searches representations, a system prompt provides instructions, and the model does not directly execute code.

questions.stem: What is the main purpose of a clear tool description?

options.A: To increase the model’s context-window size
options.B: To explain when and how the tool should be used
options.C: To give the tool permanent access to all systems
options.D: To remove the need for argument validation

questions.rationale: A tool description tells the model what the tool does, when to call it, and what its limits are. It does not change context capacity, tool permissions must remain limited, and arguments still require validation.

questions.stem: Why should every agent have a step limit?

options.A: To make every answer more creative
options.B: To increase the number of available tools
options.C: To replace monitoring and logging
options.D: To stop uncontrolled loops and repeated model calls

questions.rationale: A step limit bounds the agent loop and prevents uncontrolled cost, repeated calls, and failure to stop. It is not a creativity setting, it does not add tools, and monitoring is still required.

questions.stem: A tool cannot find employee ID E-99999. Which response is most useful for agent recovery?

options.A: {"error": "Employee not found. Valid IDs look like E-10482. Ask the user to confirm."}
options.B: An empty result with no explanation
options.C: A successful response containing an estimated employee record
options.D: A hidden exception that the model cannot read

questions.rationale: A clear structured error gives the model enough information to correct the request or ask the user for help. An empty result gives no recovery guidance, estimating a record would be unsafe and incorrect, and a hidden exception cannot help the agent recover.

questions.stem: A process always checks a form, verifies a record, asks for user approval, and then submits the request. The order never changes. Which design is most appropriate?

options.A: An autonomous agent that chooses a different path each time
options.B: A direct model call with no application workflow
options.C: A fixed workflow with an approval step before submission
options.D: A multi-agent system with a manager and several workers

questions.rationale: The sequence is stable and known in advance, so a fixed workflow is more predictable and testable. Because submission changes an external system, the approval step should remain explicit. An autonomous agent adds unnecessary variability, a direct model call cannot manage the controlled process, and a multi-agent design adds complexity without solving a real requirement.

questions.stem: What is the main purpose of rate limiting?

options.A: To make the model’s writing more consistent
options.B: To control how much service one user can consume
options.C: To improve the semantic quality of embeddings
options.D: To convert synchronous work into a queue

questions.rationale: Rate limiting restricts the amount of service one user may consume during a defined period. It does not control writing style, it does not improve embeddings, and a queue is used for asynchronous work.

questions.stem: A production request is slow. Engineers need to know what happened, where the time was spent, and whether the problem is increasing over time. Which information should the system record?

options.A: Logs, traces, and metrics
options.B: Prompts, temperature, and answer style
options.C: Chunks, embeddings, and document titles
options.D: Fine-tuning data, model weights, and training loss

questions.rationale: The team needs three kinds of operational information: logs for what happened, traces for where time was spent, and metrics for behavior over time. Prompt settings do not provide operational visibility, retrieval data is not production observability, and training information does not explain an individual production request.

questions.stem: A model provider returns a temporary timeout. Which response is most appropriate?

options.A: Rebuild the complete vector index.
options.B: Fine-tune the model on timeout examples.
options.C: Repeat the request forever until it succeeds.
options.D: Use a limited retry with increasing delay.

questions.rationale: A temporary failure may be retried a limited number of times with increasing and slightly randomized delay. Rebuilding the index is unrelated, fine-tuning cannot repair a temporary timeout, and unlimited retry can create a loop and increase load.

questions.stem: A RAG system has already indexed its documents. What is the correct flow after receiving a user question?

options.A: Generate answer → embed question → retrieve chunks → add citations
options.B: Retrieve chunks → generate answer → embed question → rerank results
options.C: Process question → retrieve and rerank chunks → assemble context → generate answer
options.D: Assemble context → process question → generate answer → retrieve chunks

questions.rationale: At query time, the system processes the question, retrieves and reranks the relevant chunks, assembles them into context, and only then generates the answer. Generating before retrieving leaves the answer ungrounded in evidence, and assembling context before processing the question skips retrieval entirely.

questions.stem: A fluent and confident answer can still be unsupported by a real source.

options.A: True
options.B: False

questions.rationale: True. A language model can produce fluent and confident text without factual support. Clear writing is not evidence that an answer is correct.

questions.stem: A high vector-similarity score proves that a retrieved passage contains the answer to the user’s question.

options.A: True
options.B: False

questions.rationale: False. A high vector-similarity score shows related meaning, but it does not prove that the passage answers the question. This tests the distinction between semantic similarity and answer relevance.

questions.stem: In agentic RAG, the model may decide whether another retrieval step is needed.

options.A: True
options.B: False

questions.rationale: True. In agentic RAG, retrieval is available as a tool. The model may decide whether to search, what to search for, and whether another search is required.

questions.stem: Streaming can make a response feel faster even when the total generation time remains unchanged.

options.A: True
options.B: False

questions.rationale: True. Streaming shows the output as it is generated. This improves perceived responsiveness, although the time required to finish the complete answer may remain unchanged.

questions.stem: Security testing performed only in English is sufficient for a system that also serves Arabic users.

options.A: True
options.B: False

questions.rationale: False. Security testing must be performed in every language the system serves, including Arabic. A control that works in English may fail when prompts, retrieved content, or attacks are written in another language.

questions.stem: Before an employee’s question is sent to the model, which component should verify the employee’s identity and permissions?

options.A: The embedding model
options.B: The application or API
options.C: The language model
options.D: The vector index

questions.rationale: Identity, authorization, and business rules belong to the application layer, not to the language model. The embedding model represents text for semantic search, the model must not determine authenticated identity or permission, and the vector index stores searchable representations without authenticating users.

questions.stem: Which architecture best supports answers from current policies with the document name and page?

options.A: A direct model call
options.B: Fine-tuning the model
options.C: A standard RAG system
options.D: A calculator tool

questions.rationale: RAG is the best starting architecture when answers must come from current approved documents and include source citations. A direct call does not reliably provide current private policy evidence, fine-tuning does not provide document and page citations by itself, and a calculator performs arithmetic rather than policy retrieval.

questions.stem: An employee confirms that an objection should be submitted. What should happen next?

options.A: The application validates the request, checks permission, runs an allowed tool, and records the action.
options.B: The model writes directly to the objection system without another check.
options.C: The retriever changes the policy index to include the objection.
options.D: The vector database submits the objection using the retrieved passage.

questions.rationale: Confirmation is important, but the application must still validate the request, verify permission, execute only an allowed tool, and record the action. The model does not directly execute external actions, the retrieval index should not be changed to submit an objection, and a vector database retrieves content rather than performing the business action.

questions.stem: Many employees ask the same common policy questions at the same time. Which design best reduces repeated cost while protecting system capacity?

options.A: Route every request to the largest model and allow longer answers.
options.B: Increase top-k and send more policy passages with every request.
options.C: Use an autonomous agent with more steps for every question.
options.D: Cache safe repeated answers and apply rate limits to users.

questions.rationale: Caching avoids repeating safe identical work, while rate limiting prevents one user from consuming too much shared capacity. A larger model and longer answers increase cost and delay, more retrieved passages increase tokens and latency, and more agent steps make cost less predictable.

questions.stem: A Finance-only document contains text claiming that every reader is authorized to view it. Which design provides the strongest protection?

options.A: Accept the claim because the document was retrieved from the index.
options.B: Filter retrieval using authenticated permissions and treat document text as data, not instructions.
options.C: Let the model decide whether the employee appears to work in Finance.
options.D: Generate the answer first and remove private details afterward.

questions.rationale: The document’s claim is untrusted text and may be an indirect prompt-injection attempt. Access must be enforced using the authenticated session before unauthorized content enters the model’s context. Retrieval does not make document instructions trustworthy, permission must not be inferred by the model, and removing sensitive details after generation is not access control.
